newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO says peace talks with Israel in crisis.
newsitem.headline: PLO says peace talks with Israel in crisis.

text.p: The Palestinian Authority said on Saturday that U.S.-brokered peace talks with Israel were in crisis and appealed to the international community to save Middle East peace deals.

"There is a crisis in the Israeli-Palestinian talks as a result of the Israeli insistence to reject adhering to signed agreements," the Authority said in a cabinet statement. "If the international community does not move immediately to save the peace process...then the whole region will witness explosions."
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat convened his cabinet in self-ruled Gaza after returning from talks in Cairo with Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak.
"The talks are close to a dead-end after the Israeli government has revealed its true positions and intentions towards the entire peace process," the statement said.

It said Israel's demand to delay by two years completion of planned troop pullbacks from the West Bank violated a 1995 interim peace deal committing Israel to withdraw from most of the occupied territory by September 1997.
"The Israeli government is trying to give a false image to the Americans and the rest of the world that it is committed to the peace process," the statement said.
